heading: Choose a service language
body:
A service is a file client/services/<Name>Service.js, .ts or .dart. You can also write it as <Name>Service.rs, .go, .rb, .lua, .py, .swift, .kt, .java, .cs, .fs or .hpp (C++) in the same folder. A component holds only its tac.html and tac.css. A page holds only its own tac.html, which places components. JavaScript and TypeScript run on every target. Dart compiles to WebAssembly with garbage collection (WasmGC), which ships wherever that bundle ships (ADR 0033; an ADR is an architecture decision record). WasmGC needs Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120 or Safari 18.2 and newer. Dart's loader also imports the JavaScript exception tag (WebAssembly.JSTag), so Dart needs Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 131 or Safari 18.4 and newer. An older browser shows a clear error instead of the Dart, Kotlin or Java services.

A Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin or Java service with no browser sibling compiles to WebAssembly. It runs as WebAssembly on the web and on any target that does not link it (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045, ADR 0073, ADR 0078, ADR 0082, ADR 0083). Kotlin compiles to WasmGC, like Dart, and needs only WasmGC: Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120 or Safari 18.2 and newer. Java compiles to WasmGC too, with TeaVM (a compiler from Java bytecode to WebAssembly); no host links Java, so a Java service runs as WebAssembly on every target. A Java web service has fields, methods with arguments, @OnStart and @OnStop, saved @LocalState and @SessionState fields, models from client/models (records, classes with fields, and enums), events with ApplicationEventPublisher and @OnEvent, Topic streams, the built-in browser cache and Store (Cached, UpdateCache, ClearCache and AllOrNothing), Tachyon's browser APIs (Clock, SecureRandom, Connectivity, PageVisibility, Preferences, Clipboard, Share, Notifications and Geolocation) with their built-in events, and the behavior annotations such as Retry, MaxAtOnce, configuration binding and validation. Groovy stays a Yon language only, because its runtime cannot be compiled to WebAssembly.

When a service has files in several languages, a JavaScript, TypeScript or Dart file wins, and so does a native service that the target links. Otherwise Tachyon uses the first WebAssembly file in this order: Rust, Go, C# or F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Ruby, Lua, Python. An F# file takes the place of C#.

A release build makes the Kotlin program about three times smaller with Binaryen, as Kotlin's own production build does. Every other WebAssembly language also gets the compiler and settings that make the smallest download: TinyGo for Go, a size-tuned rustc for Rust, -Osize and Binaryen for Swift, TeaVM and Binaryen for Java, a trimmed .NET interpreter for C# and F#, and -O4 for Dart (see WebAssembly compilers per language). A Swift program holds the Swift standard library, about 3.4 MB (0.9 MB with Brotli), so a Swift web service should not import Foundation, which would make it more than ten times larger. It does not need it: models in client/models cross the page boundary through Codable, with an encoder and decoder that Tachyon ships in the Swift program.

No target links Go, so a Go service runs as WebAssembly on every target. A C++ service is a header-only .hpp file with one class, compiled with Emscripten; no target links C++ either, so it runs as WebAssembly everywhere. Its markers are standard attributes, such as `class [[Service]] OrderService`, and Tachyon ships C#-shaped JSON and HTTP types for it (`tachyon::json`, `tachyon::http`; ADR 0099). A Ruby service runs on Tachyon's mruby WebAssembly runtime on every target (ADR 0054). Your machine builds that runtime once with Ruby and Emscripten. A Lua service runs on Tachyon's Lua 5.4 WebAssembly runtime on every target (ADR 0085). Your machine builds that runtime once with Emscripten. Native services link on their supported targets: Rust on desktop, iOS and Android, Swift on Apple, Kotlin on Android and C# on Windows. On every other target they run as WebAssembly, so every service language reaches every target. A Python service runs in the page on Pyodide 314.0.7, a Python runtime for WebAssembly (ADR 0093). Lua, Python and C++ services have limits; "Which languages can I use?" lists them. PHP and Groovy are not Tac service languages.

This site is a complete example of the web mix. Rust holds the contents list and page links. Go holds the feature catalogue and the inline code in prose. Ruby holds the navigation drawer. C# holds the documentation index. F# holds counts such as "1 feature" or "12 features". Java holds the choice of install command and the saved platform choice. Dart holds the sidebar and pager. Kotlin holds the feature pages and the place of each guide in the reading order. Swift holds the word and group filters of the feature list. Lua holds the reading time. TypeScript holds the clipboard, the guide pages, the list of Yon examples and the code showcase. JavaScript holds search and the code examples. A page loads the runtime of a language only when one of its views uses a service in that language, so the Swift program (about 0.9 MB with Brotli) loads only on the feature list.

A unit test in the same language tests each service. Content that is only data is not a service at all. Examples are the pillars, FAQ, footer and quickstart. This content lives in client/shared/data, and a view reads it as data.<name> (ADR 0036).
